summary: Andrei Ivanovich Vostrikov (1904–1937) was a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy (also known as Theodore Stcherbatsky).
Andrew B. Irvine works in philosophy and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Boston University and was an assistant professor of philosophy at Maryville College (attested 2009).

Andrew Glass specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Bukkyo University (2003) and the University of Washington (MA to 2000, PhD to 2006 under Richard Salomon and Collett Cox), also studying with Mark Allon, Ulrich Pagel, and others.
Andrew J. Nicholson specializes in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under traditional teacher Shree Narayan Mishra and held a post at Stony Brook University.

Andrew Olendzki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Lancaster University. He served as executive director of the Insight Meditation Society, executive director and resident scholar at the Barre Center for Buddhist Studies (attested 2003–2014), and senior scholar at the Mind & Life Institute (attested 2014).

Andrew P. Tuck is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Princeton University and was taught by Victor Preller, Jeffrey Stout, William E. Kennick, Robert A. F. Thurman, Daniel H. H. Ingalls, and Richard Rorty, among others.

Andrew Quintman is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Jay L. Garfield. He served as an assistant professor in the Department of Religious Studies at Yale University (attested 2015).
Andrew William Kennedy works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Leeds (attested 2006), where he was supervised by Philip A. Mellor and Kim Knott.

Andrey Klebanov specializes in Indology and linguistics. He earned his MA (to 2010) and PhD (to 2016) at the University of Hamburg under Harunaga Isaacson and Dominic Goodall, later becoming a professor at Kyoto University (attested 2019).

Andrey Terentyev (born 1948) works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the Faculty of Philosophy at Saint Petersburg State University (~1969–1975) and held a post at the Museum of the History of Religion.

Andrzej Gawroński (1885–1927) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Lviv University (~1902–1903) and Leipzig University (~1903–1907), later holding posts at Jagiellonian University (~1916–1917) and Lviv University (~1917–1927).

András Róna-Tas (born 1931) is a scholar in linguistics, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University (1950–1955), served as a visiting lecturer at the University of Vienna (1983–1984), and was President of the International Association for Tibetan Studies (~1985–1995).

André Bareau (1921–1993) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at the University of Paris, EPHE (under Jean Filliozat), and Collège de France. He held posts at the CNRS (1947), EPHE (from 1956), and Collège de France (director, 1971–1991).

André Couture (born 1945) works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Laval University, the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and Paris-Sorbonne University (~1972–1977), and held a post at Laval University (~1980).

André Padoux (1920–2017) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Paris and under Lakshman Joo, Olivier Lacombe, and Louis Renou. He directed the Institut Français Frankfurt (~1959–1964) and served at the CNRS (1959, 1982).

Andy Rotman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and the University of Chicago under Sheldon Pollock and Steven Collins. He held a post at Smith College (attested 2013–2017).

Angela Falco Howard is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. She completed her doctoral dissertation at the Institute of Fine Arts, NYU, under Alexander Coburn Soper, and became a professor at Rutgers University (attested 2005).
Angela Manderscheid is a scholar in Tibetology who held posts at the Free University of Berlin and as a researcher at the University of Oulu (attested 1998).

Angela Sumegi specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She studied under Nalini Devdas, earned a PhD at the University of Ottawa, and served as an assistant professor at Carleton University's College of the Humanities (attested 2008).

Angelo De Gubernatis (1840–1913) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Turin and under Albrecht Weber at Humboldt University of Berlin. He held professorships at the University of Florence (1863–1891) and Sapienza University of Rome (1890).
